recommendations.raw_text: Staff passkey management on admin-api: list own passkeys, add a second (backup) device-bound key with a fresh aal3 re-authentication, remove one (never the last); and an ADM reset of another staff member's passkeys with a reason and four-eyes (the next sign-in then enrols again with password + emailed code). plan.why: With one device-bound key per person, a lost key locks a staff member out and needs SQL on the server (R-08); OQ-14 plans two keys each, which needs "add a backup key". Design decided in DQ-04 (2026-11-13): own recovery codes, requester proof (password + code + emailed code), two ADM approvals in the console with an out-of-band check, 72-hour restriction, break glass on the server. Split into S16a (signed-in part) and S16b (recovery flow).

scale.P0: Pilot blocker: a security or privacy defect, a legal obligation, or a state staff cannot get out of without SQL on the server.
scale.P1: Pilot operations: a pilot flow or a Docs/23 Must screen cannot be done in the console, or a server-side safety rule is missing; a console workaround may exist but is weak.
scale.P2: Completeness and efficiency: Docs/23 Should items, extra filters and context, aggregates; the console has a working workaround.
scale.P3: Tied to a later feature (the AI build).

complexity_scale.S: ~1 point: one read operation, or a field or filter on an existing operation.
complexity_scale.M: ~2-3 points: two or three operations, or one rule plus a scheduler job, or a new column with a migration.
complexity_scale.L: ~4-6 points: a new entity with its operations, or a rule that cuts across many operations.
complexity_scale.XL: 6+ points: a cross-module rewrite with per-module conflict rules.
complexity_scale.note: Points are relative effort per the backend definition of done (Docs/40 text, registry and codegen, handler, projection, sweep resolver, happy-path + authz-negative + rule tests). Reference: backend S12 (3 new operations, 2 changed, staff tooling, contract bump) is about 9 points.

method: Closed items (BR-01..BR-06) are kept for history only.
Each open item is rated by what goes wrong without it at the pilot, not by its source label (blocker/high/must/should): the source labels described when the console needed it.
Items whose parts differ in risk are split (BR-35 row vs filters vs more-info vs correction; BR-15 actions vs redaction; BR-21 list vs notification; BR-26 ids vs notice).
Console workarounds already built (deviations D-xx) lower the priority only when they are safe; they never lower a server-side safety or privacy rule.

principles: Order: first the reads that unblock the console (S13), then the pilot blockers (privacy S14, legal S15, staff keys S16a/S16b), then pilot-operations completeness (S17-S19), then Should items (S20-S24), then closure (S25).

One stage = one working session that fits a 5-hour token window. Target load <= 11 points (backend S12 was about 9, S11 about 11). Security-sensitive or cross-module stages are planned lighter (S16a, S16b, S22, S23).

A stage groups items by module and contract area so the session reads one set of docs and code (backend conventions.context_budget: read only the listed ranges, lean on the generated registry, copy patterns from finished modules).

Every stage follows the backend definition of done per operation and ends with contract:check and openapi:check green and the console contract regenerated, so the tree is never left with a half-updated registry.
If a session runs long, stop at the stage's split_point and move the rest to S25 or the named later stage; never split inside a task.

Auth host, cp-web-admin interactions only: auth.staff_recovery_start (email, password unless password_forgotten, one recovery code) and auth.staff_recovery_verify (the emailed one-time code). The same answer and timing whatever the account state; per-account and per-IP rate limits (and the PoW of the anonymous grant where it applies); one open request per account; the recovery code is consumed when the request is created; disabled accounts never get a request. Returns an opaque request handle bound to the interaction.

Notices on creation: to the account email ("if this was not you, tell an administrator") and to every other active ADM (in-app and email; the email links to the console, nothing can be approved from it).

Admin approvals: admin.staff_recoveries_list and admin.staff_recovery_get (ADM; requester, roles, request time, IP country, password_forgotten; no codes), admin.staff_recovery_approve (fresh aal3, reason, verification_method and note; refused for the requester, for an ADM under post-recovery restriction, and twice by the same ADM) and admin.staff_recovery_reject (any ADM, reason; ends the request). Two distinct approvals move the request to approved. Also listed in admin.work_summary when S21 builds it.

Completion: auth.staff_recovery_status (by handle) and auth.staff_recovery_complete: a new password first when password_forgotten (the normal password rules), then a new device-bound key registered and proven at once (aal3). Then in one transaction: old keys, sessions and refresh tokens revoked, a new recovery-code set issued and shown once, restricted_until = now + 72 h, the account email and every ADM notified, audit entries for every step.

Post-recovery restriction: STAFF_RECOVERY_RESTRICTED on four-eyes approve, platform role grant and revoke, admin.staff_enable and admin.staff_recovery_approve while restricted_until is in the future; admin.staff_me carries restricted_until.

Tests: the full happy path (lost key, and forgotten password); no enumeration (unknown, disabled and wrong-details accounts give identical answers); rate limits; expiry at 24 h; one rejection ends the request; self-approval and double approval refused; a restricted ADM cannot approve; synced key refused at completion; sessions revoked after completion.

decisions_needed.question: Lost-key reset design (your research on the 2026-11-09 risk review): ADM reset with four-eyes and re-enrolment by password + emailed code, or something stronger (e.g. an in-person check, a waiting period)?

decisions_needed.answer: Recommended process approved (owner, 2026-11-13), replacing both the default (ADM-initiated reset with four-eyes) and the owner's first proposal (requester names two approvers, approvers type 128-character paper codes through an emailed 10-minute link).

decision.recovery_codes: Every staff account holds its own 10 single-use recovery codes: 20 characters each from Crockford base32 (no ambiguous characters, no symbols, so they can be typed on any keyboard layout), shown in groups of four (about 100 bits). Shown once when the first passkey is enrolled (and to existing staff at their next sign-in), written or printed by the staff member, stored sealed and apart from the security keys. Stored as keyed hashes (HMAC-SHA-256 with a server pepper), compared in constant time. Can be replaced after a fresh aal3 sign-in; the new set cancels the old sheet.
decision.requester_proof: Lost key: email + password + one of the account's own recovery codes + a one-time code sent to the staff email. Forgotten password as well: email + recovery code + emailed code, and the requester sets a new password at the end. The requester never names approvers. The answer is the same whether or not the account exists, is disabled or the details are wrong; attempts are rate-limited per account and per IP; one open request per account; disabled accounts cannot recover.
decision.notification: Creating a request notifies the account's email ("a recovery was requested for your account; if this was not you, tell an administrator") and every other active ADM (in-app and email). The email only links to the console; no approval is possible from a link.
decision.approvals: Two different ADMs, neither the requester, each signed in to the console with their passkey and a fresh aal3 (within 5 minutes), approve with a reason and the out-of-band check they made (call to a known number, in person, video call, other + note). Any one ADM can reject, which ends the request. Approvers under post-recovery restriction cannot approve. The whole request expires after 24 hours.
decision.completion: After two approvals the requester (same browser, holding the request handle) registers a new device-bound key (security key or Windows Hello; synced passkeys refused with PASSKEY_NOT_DEVICE_BOUND) and proves it at once (aal3). The password stays unless the request said it was forgotten. Then: old keys and all sessions and refresh tokens revoked, a new recovery-code set issued (the old sheet is void), the account email and every ADM notified, everything audited.
decision.restriction_after_recovery: For 72 hours the recovered account cannot approve four-eyes changes, grant or revoke roles, enable staff, or approve another recovery (STAFF_RECOVERY_RESTRICTED).
decision.roles: The same flow for every staff role (ADM, MOD, CRV, SUP), always with two ADM approvers (see DQ-15).
decision.break_glass: When fewer than two other ADMs are active, a documented server procedure (a staff CLI run on the server shell, with a reason, audited as actor system, all ADMs notified) disables the account's keys so the next sign-in enrols again. This replaces the "SQL on the server" fallback of R-08.
